name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu

sides.name: Viet Minh
sides.strength: About 50,000 combat troops, 50,000 logistic porters, four divisions, and the first heavy artillery the Viet Minh had massed in the field

sides.name: French Union
sides.commander: Christian de Castries (garrison), Henri Navarre (overall in Indochina)
sides.strength: About 14,000 troops including paratroopers, the French Foreign Legion, Moroccan and Algerian regiments, Thai auxiliaries, and air resupply only
sides.casualties: Roughly 2,300 killed, 5,200 wounded, and 11,700 captured (only 3,300 survived captivity to be repatriated)

summary: Navarre planted a fortified airhead in a valley near the Laotian border to lure Giap into a set-piece battle the French expected to win on firepower. Giap surprised them by dragging Soviet-supplied 105 mm howitzers and 37 mm anti-aircraft guns onto the surrounding ridges by hand, dug them into reverse slopes, and opened the siege on the thirteenth of March. The French airstrip was rendered unusable within twenty-four hours and air resupply became suicidal under the AA umbrella. The outer strongpoints (Beatrice, Gabrielle, Anne-Marie) fell within a week. The central garrison surrendered on the seventh of May after fifty-six days.
significance: Dien Bien Phu ended French rule in Indochina. The Geneva Accords of July 1954 partitioned Vietnam at the seventeenth parallel and set the table for American intervention a decade later. The battle is the canonical case of a peasant insurgency defeating a Western expeditionary force in a stand-up battle, and the strategic lesson resonated through every twentieth-century anticolonial war that followed.
